prompt: In Cucumber, what is the glue code that Karate does without?
hint: Who makes a sentence like "the customer asks for the list of shows" do anything?

choices.text: The XML that links the feature files to Maven
choices.why: Maven finds features through testResources in both tools; glue is about steps.

choices.text: A method per step sentence that performs it
choices.why: Right. Karate's steps are keywords it already knows how to perform.

choices.text: The Gherkin keywords Given, When and Then themselves
choices.why: Karate keeps those words; they are for the reader in both tools.

choices.text: The HTTP client library that sends requests to the server
choices.why: Karate has an HTTP client inside it; glue is the code that maps a sentence to an action.

prompt: Why does the pom.xml copy the non-Java files of src/test/java with a testResources block?
hint: Where does Karate look for features, and where does Maven put things?

choices.text: So that the features compile together with BoxofficeTest
choices.why: Feature files are not compiled; they are read as they are.

choices.text: So that Maven downloads Karate
choices.why: Dependencies do that; testResources only copies files.

choices.text: Maven would leave them off the classpath
choices.why: Right. Without it Karate finds no feature and runs nothing.

choices.text: So that git ignores them
choices.why: Maven has nothing to do with git.

prompt: The method in BoxofficeTest does not test anything itself; it returns tests for JUnit to run, which is what the annotation @___ says.
hint: Not @Test.

prompt: Which step of the first scenario sends the request?
hint: Nothing goes out before it.

choices.text: Given path 'v1', 'shows'
choices.why: path only adds to the address.

choices.text: * url baseUrl
choices.why: url only sets the address.

choices.text: When method get
choices.why: Right. method sends the request with everything set above it.

choices.text: Then status 200
choices.why: status checks a response that has already arrived.

prompt: A colleague rewrites every Given, When, Then and And of shows.feature as *. What changes when the feature runs?
hint: What does Karate do with those four words?

choices.text: The Then steps stop checking anything
choices.why: A check is made by status and match, not by Then.

choices.text: Karate refuses the file as invalid Gherkin
choices.why: * is valid in any position; the Background step already uses it.

choices.text: The steps run in a different order
choices.why: Steps run from the top whatever word starts them.

choices.text: Nothing about the run; only how it reads
choices.why: Right. Karate treats the four words exactly as *; they are for the reader.

prompt: The first run of the project had one JUnit class. How many tests did Surefire report?
hint: One per scenario.

prompt: Match each marker to the value it accepts.
hint: Section 04's table.

prompt: boxoffice starts sending a new field, "venue", in every show. Which scenario of match.feature fails?
hint: Which comparisons allow keys the expected value does not name?

choices.text: one show, whole, and every show has the same shape
choices.why: Right. Both compare with ==, which refuses an extra key; contains does not.

choices.text: Only the list holds the small show
choices.why: contains accepts keys it does not name; that one keeps passing.

choices.text: None of them: Karate ignores fields it was not told about
choices.why: == is strict; section 04 removed one expected key and the scenario failed.

choices.text: All four, because the shape of every answer changed
choices.why: The error scenario reads /v1/shows/sh-999, whose problem body has no venue.

prompt: Why is seats_left: '#number' a better check than seats_left: 4 in one show, whole?
hint: Who else touches the seats of the shows?

choices.text: 4 is a number Karate cannot compare
choices.why: Karate compares numbers exactly; the failure shown in section 04 printed 4.

choices.text: Other tests change it
choices.why: Right. The marker still checks the field exists and is a number; 4 would fail whenever another feature bought a seat, and that is not a defect.

choices.text: '#number' also accepts "4" as text, which is more tolerant
choices.why: It refuses "4"; a marker is still a check of the type.

choices.text: It makes the scenario run faster
choices.why: Both comparisons cost the same; the reason is what the test claims.

prompt: In orders.feature, how many token requests does a run make, and why?
hint: Read the server's log of the run.

choices.text: One: callonce shares one token across all clients
choices.why: callonce keeps the result of its own call, for ci-tests; the auditor is a different call.

choices.text: Two: callonce for ci-tests, call for auditor
choices.why: Right, which is what boxoffice logged.

choices.text: Three: the Background runs twice and the auditor asks once
choices.why: The Background runs twice, but callonce asks only the first time.

choices.text: Four
choices.why: That would be a call in the Background plus extra calls; the log shows fewer.

prompt: A scenario expected 403 and got 201 after the auditor's header step replaced configure headers. What should the tester do first?
hint: Is the server the only thing that can be wrong?

choices.text: File a defect: the auditor was allowed to buy
choices.why: The request carried the ci-tests token; the server was right to accept it.

choices.text: Change the expected status to 201
choices.why: That asserts the test's own mistake as the behaviour.

choices.text: Check what the request actually sent
choices.why: Right. The report's log shows the token that went out, and it was the wrong one.

choices.text: Restart boxoffice and run it again
choices.why: A restart puts seats back; it would not change which token the test sends.

prompt: Match each step to what it does.
hint: Section 05 sets them side by side.

pairs.right: runs the feature once per file and shares the result
headers for every request that follows
a header for the next request only

right_distractors: skips the feature when the runner meets it

prompt: Why is token.feature tagged @ignore?
hint: What would the runner do with it otherwise?

choices.text: So that its token is not printed in the report
choices.why: @ignore says nothing about printing; it is about running.

choices.text: So the runner skips it
choices.why: Right. Run alone, it has no clientId and fails.

choices.text: So that callonce is allowed to read it
choices.why: call and callonce read any feature, tagged or not.

choices.text: Because tokens expire and Karate must not cache them
choices.why: Nothing about expiry; the tag only keeps the runner from running the file alone.

prompt: In the Examples table, why does the last row write '2' with quotes?
hint: The cell is pasted into the request as it is written.

choices.text: Karate requires quotes around numbers in a table
choices.why: The rows 0, 1, 6 and 7 have none and work.

choices.text: To send the string "2" rather than the number 2
choices.why: Right. It is a different input, and boxoffice refuses it with 422.

choices.text: To stop Karate from adding it to the previous row
choices.why: Rows are separate; nothing is added up.

choices.text: Because 2 seats is already tested in orders.feature
choices.why: orders.feature buys 2 seats of sh-101; the quotes are about the type sent.

prompt: Each run of seats.feature buys 7 seats of sh-102, which has 120. On which run in a row, without a restart, does the six-seat row first get 409?
hint: Seventeen runs use 119 seats.

prompt: Order the rows of the seats table from the smallest value sent to the largest, as a boundary analysis lays them out.
hint: The rule is 1 to 6.

prompt: Where do you find the request and the response of the step that failed?
hint: Karate writes two records of a run.

choices.text: In the SLF4J lines at the top of the terminal output
choices.why: Those only say there is no logging back end.

choices.text: In boxoffice's terminal
choices.why: boxoffice logs one line per request, with no headers or body.

choices.text: In pom.xml
choices.why: The pom describes the build; it records no run.

choices.text: In the step's log
choices.why: Right: on the feature's page in target/karate-reports, headers included.

prompt: How many tests did the full run report?
hint: One per scenario, and per row of an outline.

prompt: A pipeline runs mvn test '-Dkarate.options=--tags @smok' and stays green for a month. What is the likeliest story?
hint: Look at the spelling, then at section 07.

choices.text: boxoffice had no defect that month
choices.why: HEAD still answers 405; a suite that ran would have said so.

choices.text: No scenario carries @smok, so every run had 0 tests
choices.why: Right. Tests run: 0 is a green build, and only reading the count catches it.

choices.text: Karate ignores --tags when it is misspelled and runs everything
choices.why: It selects by the tag given; a misspelt tag selects nothing.

choices.text: The SLF4J warning hid the failures
choices.why: The warning is three lines about logging; failures are printed in full.

prompt: You want one scenario that checks every order boxoffice returns has the same shape, whatever its id and total. Which match fits?
hint: Markers for what changes, == for the rest.

choices.text: match response == { id: 'ord-1001', total_cents: 16000 }
choices.why: Fixed values tie the test to one order, and == then fails on the keys it leaves out.

choices.text: match response contains { status: 'confirmed' }
choices.why: That checks one field and lets any other shape through.

choices.text: match response == { id: '#regex ord-[0-9]+', show_id: '#string', seats: '#number', total_cents: '#number', status: '#string', payment: '#string' }
choices.why: Right. Every key is named, so an extra or missing one fails, and markers stand where values change.

choices.text: match response == '#ignore'
choices.why: That accepts anything at all, which checks no shape.

prompt: Lesson 7's OrdersTest and this lesson's orders.feature test the same rules. What does the Karate version check that the Java one did not?
hint: Compare the checks on the 201.

choices.text: That a request without a token is refused
choices.why: The Java class had noTokenIs401AndSaysWhy; the Karate feature has no such scenario.

choices.text: That the auditor may not buy
choices.why: Both have it: theAuditorMayReadButNotBuy and the auditor scenario.

choices.text: The new order's whole body
choices.why: Right. The Java test checked total_cents and the location; the feature's == checks every key.

choices.text: That seven seats are refused
choices.why: That was sevenSeatsAreRefused in Java, and seats.feature here.

prompt: Which of these would make the full run report a number other than 16?
hint: What counts as a test?

choices.text: Adding a seventh row to the Examples table
choices.why: Right: every row is a test.

choices.text: Removing @ignore from token.feature
choices.why: Right: the runner would then run it as a test of its own, and it would fail.

choices.text: Changing callonce to call in the Background
choices.why: That changes how many token requests are sent, not how many scenarios run.

choices.text: Deleting the testResources block from pom.xml
choices.why: Right: Karate would find no feature, and the count would drop to zero.
